claude.sample_unit: generated outputs (100 synthetic vignettes x 3 seeds x 4 conditions)

links.outcome: Unsupported claim rate with RAG over raw clinical text versus baseline LLM
links.effect: Unsupported claims rose from 5.0% (95% CI 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI 40.1–47.2%) with retrieval, an 8.7-fold increase (p<0.001, d=2.31).
links.quote: RAG substantially increased hallucination: unsupported claim rates rose from 5.0% (95% CI: 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI: 40.1–47.2%) with retrieval—an 8.7-fold increase (  p < 0.001, Cohen’s  d = 2.31).

unlisted_practices: Compiling heterogeneous patient data into structured machine-readable artifacts with explicit provenance tracking before generation
Multi-step agent workflow with verification and constraint checking
Requiring citations in generated clinical outputs

links.outcome: unsupported claim rate with raw RAG
links.quote: RAG substantially increased hallucination: unsupported claim rates rose from 5.0% (95% CI: 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI: 40.1–47.2%) with retrieval—an 8.7-fold increase (  p < 0.001, Cohen’s  d = 2.31).

links.outcome: unsupported claim rate with structured artifacts
links.effect: Unsupported claims were 8.4% (95% CI: 6.7–10.3%), reported as 40% relative reduction versus baseline; p = 0.02; d = 0.48.
links.quote: Structured artifacts reduced unsupported claims to 8.4% (95% CI: 6.7–10.3%) in single-pass generation, a 40% relative reduction versus baseline (  p = 0.02,  d = 0.48).

links.effect: Agent workflow had 21.1% unsupported claims and lowest contraindication miss rate (0.04).
links.quote: The agent workflow achieved 21.1% unsupported claims with the lowest contraindication miss rate (0.04) and highest clinician utility scores.

screen.practice: retrieval grounding vs structured artifact representation and agentic verification guardrails
screen.reason: Evaluates and compares deployment guardrails and grounding approaches (RAG vs structured patient artifacts vs multi-step agent verification with constraint checking) on hallucination rates and clinical safety using synthetic patient vignettes.
